topics.label: Lecture introduction and framing
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture topic and sets expectations regarding the complexity of complement nomenclature.

topics.label: Complement system overview and fundamental concepts
topics.groupedBecause: They introduce the fundamental principles and mechanics that govern how the complement system operates.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: They describe the recognition pathways that initiate the complement cascade and converge on activating C3 on pathogen surfaces.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: They explain the mechanisms by which activated complement eliminates pathogens and recruits immune responses.

topics.label: Regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement from inadvertently attacking and destroying host cells.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: It details the distinct clinical manifestations and disease risks resulting from deficiencies in various complement components.

topics.label: Microbial evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: It examines the strategies pathogens use to circumvent complement-mediated destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary example.

topics.label: Closing remarks
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture and previews the next topic in the lecture series.
